examples.solution_text:
The bottom is the total of the two horizontal lengths above it.
$\begin{aligned}x&=3+5\\&=8\text{ m}\end{aligned}$
The two vertical lengths on the right add to the left side.
$\begin{aligned}y&=6-2\\&=4\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

The two upper horizontal lengths add to the bottom length.
$5+x=13$
$\begin{aligned}x&=13-5\\&=8\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

(a) The three horizontal lengths along the bottom add to the top length.
$8+x+10=27$
$\begin{aligned}x&=27-18\\&=9\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$
(b) The matching dashes show that the other bottom side is also $8\text{ m}$.
$8+x+8=29$
$\begin{aligned}x&=29-16\\&=13\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

Trace the boundary from the bottom-left corner, starting along the bottom to the right. The $9\text{ cm}$ side and $x$ run right; the $4\text{ cm}$ step and $15\text{ cm}$ top run left.
$9+x=4+15$
$\begin{aligned}x&=19-9\\&=10\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

The horizontal lengths give the width of the gap, not its depth.
$24-6-10=8\text{ cm}$
No length is given for the depth of the gap. It could change while the marked lengths stay the same, so $x$ cannot be found.

examples.derivation: Horizontal balance gives x=3+5=8 m; vertical balance gives y=6−2=4 m. Both agree with the diagram.
The upper horizontal lengths satisfy 5+x=13, so x=8 cm, matching the drawn segment.

(a) Horizontal balance gives 8+x+10=27, so x=27−18=9 cm. (b) Matching marks identify two 8 m bottom segments; 8+x+8=29 gives x=29−16=13 m. The repaired strokes cross the side midpoints at (4,0) and (25,0). Each spans 1.8 coordinate units, approximately 8.2 pt at scale 0.16, with identical 0.8 pt widths.
